# AI HANDOFF — STEAL A MONSTER

> **To any AI continuing this project:** read this whole file first, then
> `README.md` (features and controls) and `TESTING.md` (what is verified).
> **Keep this file up to date**: when you finish a change, update the
> "Current state" and "Change log" sections below, so the next AI (or the
> previous one, coming back after a usage limit) can continue without
> guessing.
>
> **Untuk pemilik game (Bahasa Indonesia):** berikan file ini (atau seluruh
> folder `steal-a-monster`, atau link GitHub-nya) ke AI lain, lalu tulis
> permintaanmu seperti biasa. Untuk AI yang hanya menerima upload file, unduh
> **satu file HTML berisi seluruh game**:
> https://kenshirodaniel8-bit.github.io/minecraft-realistis/source.html
> (selalu versi terbaru; klik kanan → *Save as*), lalu upload ke AI itu. Bilang ke AI itu: *"Baca AI-HANDOFF.md dulu, dan
> perbarui file itu setelah selesai."*

---

## 1. What this is

A 3D multiplayer browser game: explore islands, fight and recruit cute baby
monsters, put them in your base tower for income, steal other players'
monsters and protect your own.

- **Owner:** GitHub user `kenshirodaniel8-bit`, repository
  `kenshirodaniel8-bit/minecraft-realistis`. The game lives in the
  **`steal-a-monster/`** folder (the repository root is a different,
  older project called "Realistis" — don't touch it).
- **Working branch:** `claude/steal-a-monster-game-mjo51w` (all work so far
  is there; not merged into `main`). Don't open pull requests unless the
  owner asks.
- **Live site (single-player + online rooms):**
  https://kenshirodaniel8-bit.github.io/minecraft-realistis/ — published
  automatically by `.github/workflows/steal-a-monster-pages.yml` on every
  push to the working branch (or `main`) that touches `steal-a-monster/**`.
  CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs `npm test`.
- **The owner speaks Indonesian.** Reply in Indonesian, simple words, step by
  step for anything they must click themselves. **In-game text is English.**
  User guides for the owner are in Indonesian (`PANDUAN-FIREBASE.md`).

## 2. Tech and architecture

- **Client:** Three.js (`three@0.186.1`), plain ES modules, no framework,
  everything procedural (no model or texture files). `public/`.
- **Server:** Node.js ≥ 20, Express + Socket.IO, **server-authoritative**
  `Game` class (`server/game.js`) with services in `server/services/`.
  Clients only send intentions (move, attack, buy…); the server decides
  Money, damage, ownership.
- **Shared code:** `shared/` (imported as `#shared/...`), identical on server
  and client: config, world generation, species, swords, costumes, guards,
  names.
- **Three ways to run the same game code:**
  1. `npm start` — Node server (`server.js`), saves in `DATA_DIR` (JSON files).
  2. **Web build** (`node scripts/build-web.mjs` → `dist-web/`) — the whole
     `Game` runs **inside the browser** (`public/client/localNet.js`), saves
     in IndexedDB/localStorage (`browserStore.js`). This is what GitHub Pages
     serves.
  3. **Online rooms** (web build + Firebase): the room creator's browser runs
     the `Game`; guests talk to it through **Firebase Realtime Database**
     (`public/client/rooms.js`). Accounts use **Firebase Authentication**
     (`public/client/accounts.js`, `fb.js`).
- **Message flow:** client `net.request(type, payload)` → `game.handle(sid,
  type, payload)` → `game.handlers[type]` → service method returning
  `{ ok: true, ... }` or `fail('code', 'message')`. Broadcasts go out with
  `game.broadcast` / `broadcastNear` / `send`.

### Key files

| Area | Files |
|---|---|
| Game loop, join/leave, snapshots, handlers | `server/game.js` |
| Profiles, sanitising, ownership ledger | `server/services/playerData.js`, `server/storage.js` |
| Combat, monsters AI | `server/services/combat.js`, `monsterAI.js` |
| Bases, income, guards purchase | `server/services/bases.js` |
| Guards + helicopters AI | `server/services/guards.js`, `shared/guards.js`, client `guardsView.js` |
| Costumes, Legend Master powers | `server/services/costumes.js`, `shared/costumes.js`, client `humanoid.js`, `legendFx.js`, `effects.js` |
| Admin (Player panel, return, ban) | `server/services/admin.js`, client `ui.js` (`playersHtml`), `main.js` actions |
| Accounts | Node: `server/accounts.js`; online: `public/client/accounts.js`; names: `shared/names.js` |
| Online rooms | `public/client/rooms.js`, `firebase-database.rules.json`, `public/firebase-config.js` |
| Client entry, controls, events | `public/client/main.js` |
| HUD and panels | `public/client/ui.js`, `public/index.html`, `public/style.css` |
| World and monsters | `shared/world.js`, `shared/monsters.js`, `shared/speciesGen.js`, `public/client/worldRenderer.js`, `monsterRenderer.js` |

## 3. Commands

```bash
cd steal-a-monster
npm install
npm start                      # http://localhost:3000
npm test                       # 86 unit/integration tests (node --test), must stay green
npm run test:e2e               # 2 real browsers vs the Node server (Playwright + Chromium)
node scripts/build-web.mjs     # web build -> dist-web/ (what GitHub Pages serves, incl. source.html)
node scripts/build-handoff-html.mjs   # ONE html file with these docs + all source -> steal-a-monster-for-ai.html

# Online rooms / accounts against the official Firebase emulators (needs Java):
npx firebase-tools@13 emulators:start --only auth,database --project demo-sam &
node scripts/room-e2e.mjs 127.0.0.1:9000 127.0.0.1:9099
node scripts/rules-check.mjs   # security rules: who may write what
```

`DEV_COMMANDS=1 npm start` enables chat cheats (`/money N`, `/level N`, `/tp X Z`, …).
Browser tests use SwiftShader (software WebGL): frame rates there are
meaningless; to inspect visuals, freeze effects and take screenshots.

## 4. Rules for changing the code

1. **Run `npm test` before every commit.** Add a test in `tests/` for new
   server rules (see existing suites; `tests/helpers.js` has a fake clock,
   `h.join`, `h.place`, `h.advance`, `h.spawnMonster`).
2. **New message type** → add it to `game.handlers` in `server/game.js`. The
   test "every message the game handles is reachable" calls each one with a
   bogus payload, so validate input (`server/validate.js`) and never throw.
   If it spends Money, use `s.recall(reqId)` / `s.remember(reqId, res)` for
   idempotency and add it to `TRANSACTIONAL` in `public/client/rooms.js`.
3. **New profile field** → sanitise it in `sanitizeProfile`
   (`server/services/playerData.js`), give it a default in `newProfile`.
   Saves from old versions must still load.
4. **Admin names live in TWO places** and must match: `ADMIN_NAMES` in
   `shared/names.js` **and** the email list in `firebase-database.rules.json`
   (`<name>@players.steal-a-monster.game`, lowercase, spaces → dots). After
   changing the rules file, the **owner must paste it again** in Firebase
   Console → Realtime Database → Rules → Publish (you cannot do it).
5. Prices and numbers belong in `shared/` (`config.js`, `costumes.js`,
   `guards.js`, `weapons.js`), not hard-coded in services.
6. After changing the web game, the live site updates by itself after the
   push (1–3 minutes). Tell the owner to press **Ctrl + F5**.
7. Commit messages: plain English, describe what changed for players. Push
   with `git push -u origin claude/steal-a-monster-game-mjo51w`.
8. Update `README.md` / `TESTING.md` / this file when features change.
9. If you work from the single HTML file (`source.html`) instead of the
   repository, give the owner back **complete files with their paths**, so
   they (or the next AI with GitHub access) can put them in place.

## 5. Firebase (online rooms and accounts)

- Project **`steal-a-monster`** (region asia-southeast1). Config is in
  `public/firebase-config.js` (public by design; the rules protect the data).
- **Authentication → Email/Password** is enabled (done by the owner).
  Accounts are made **in the game** with *Create account*: the game turns the
  name into an email `name@players.steal-a-monster.game` (lowercase, spaces →
  dots). Users added by hand in the Firebase console with Gmail addresses are
  **not** game accounts.
- Existing game accounts (Oct 2026): `daniel`, `prabu`, `shallom`, `naddd`
  (Nadine's account).
- Database layout: `sam/accounts/<uid>` `{name, profile (JSON string), at,
  online}`, `sam/bans/<uid>` `{name, at}`, `sam/returns/<uid>/<id>` `{j}`,
  `sam/rooms/<CODE>` (`host`, `guests`, `up`, `down`).
- **The rules must be published by the owner** whenever
  `firebase-database.rules.json` changes. Give them the full file content in a
  code block plus: *Realtime Database → Rules → hapus semua → tempel →
  Publish*.
- Unban: delete `sam/bans/<uid>` in the console (Realtime Database → Data).
- Free Spark plan: ~10 GB/month download; one guest ≈ 80 MB/hour.

FILE: README.md

# STEAL A MONSTER

A 3D multiplayer browser game about **adorable baby monsters**. Explore a big
blocky world, battle wild monsters with your sword, **pay to recruit** the
ones you defeat, show them off in your base where they earn Money — and keep
rival players from walking in and stealing them.

Built from scratch with **Three.js** (client) and **Node.js + Express +
Socket.IO** (server). Not a Roblox game: no Roblox Studio, APIs or Luau.

![The monster roster](docs/screenshots/gallery.png)

**FIND → BATTLE → DEFEAT → PAY → RECRUIT → RETURN TO BASE → COLLECT → PROTECT (or STEAL)**

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Out in the plains](docs/screenshots/plains.jpg) | ![A defeated monster and its recruit card](docs/screenshots/battle.jpg) |
| ![A base full of monsters earning Money](docs/screenshots/base.jpg) | ![LUCKY LUCKY event with Lucky Blocks](docs/screenshots/lucky-lucky.jpg) |
| ![Monster inspector](docs/screenshots/inspect.jpg) | ![World map](docs/screenshots/map.jpg) |

![Five of the monsters up close](docs/screenshots/gallery-closeup.jpg)

*Screenshots are from headless Chromium with software rendering
(`node scripts/screenshots.mjs`).*

---

## Play in the browser (no install)

**https://kenshirodaniel8-bit.github.io/minecraft-realistis/** — the
single-player web version. The whole game, including the game-server logic,
runs inside your browser; progress is saved in that browser. It is published
automatically to the `gh-pages` branch by `.github/workflows/steal-a-monster-pages.yml`
(build it yourself with `node scripts/build-web.mjs`, output in `dist-web/`).
If the link shows a 404, enable Pages once: repository **Settings → Pages →
Deploy from a branch → `gh-pages` / (root)**.

### Online rooms with friends (Firebase)

The web version can also be played **online with friends** without running a
server: one player presses **Create room** and sends the invite link; friends
open it and press **Join**. The room creator's browser runs the game (the same
server code), and all messages travel through a free **Firebase Realtime
Database**. To switch it on, follow the step-by-step guide (in Indonesian):
**[PANDUAN-FIREBASE.md](PANDUAN-FIREBASE.md)** — create a Firebase project,
publish [`firebase-database.rules.json`](firebase-database.rules.json), and
paste the web config into `public/firebase-config.js`.

Online rooms need an **account** (Firebase Authentication with
Email/Password must be switched on, see the guide). Every player's progress is
saved in **their own account**, so the monsters you get in a friend's room are
still yours in your own game and in every other room.

Limits: the room closes when its creator leaves; every message goes through Firebase (about 100–300 ms
extra delay); a guest downloads about 22 KB/s, so the free plan (10 GB/month)
covers roughly 100 hours a month with one friend. It was tested with the
official Firebase Realtime Database emulator and the real Firebase SDK
(`scripts/room-e2e.mjs`), not against a live Firebase project.

For a dedicated server instead (lowest lag, progress saved on the server), use
the Node.js server below, hosted somewhere everyone can reach.

### Accounts

The title screen has **Log in** and **Create account** (name + password of at
least 6 characters). Names are **unique** — "Mira Fox", "mira fox" and
"Mira   Fox" are the same name — 2–16 letters, numbers, **spaces**, `_` or
`-`. Logged in, your monsters, Money and everything else follow you: into your
friends' rooms, into your own room and onto other devices. Every time you
create or join a server you are asked **"start over from the beginning, or
continue with your progress from before?"** (starting over really wipes the
account's progress). **Play without an account** still works for single-player
on one device.

- **Web build / online rooms:** Firebase Authentication (the email is made from
  the name, `mira.fox@players.steal-a-monster.game`, nobody types an email) and
  the account's profile in the Realtime Database at `sam/accounts/<uid>`. The
  database rules let only the owner write their account and check the name
  against the login.
- **Node server:** accounts live on the server in `DATA_DIR/accounts.json`
  (scrypt password hashes). The browser keeps a "remember me" key instead of the
  password.

### The admins: Daniel, Nadine, Prabu and Shallom

The accounts named **Daniel**, **Nadine** (also **naddd**, her account), **Prabu** and **Shallom** are the
admins of **every** server and room (register them first so nobody else takes
the names; capitals don't matter). Only the admins get a
**🛡 Player** button. It lists everyone in the server, which monsters they stole
and **from whom**, with two buttons:

- **↩ Return to <owner>** — the stolen monster goes back to its owner (straight
  into their base if they are online, otherwise it waits in their account and
  arrives the next time they play);
- **⛔ Ban** — the thief is kicked with "You were banned by the admin." and
  can't come back (Node server: `DATA_DIR/bans.json`; online: `sam/bans/<uid>`).

To lift a ban, delete the player's entry from `bans.json` (Node) or from
`sam/bans` in the Firebase console (online). An admin can't ban themselves or another admin. The list is `ADMIN_NAMES` in
`shared/names.js` and the same four emails in `firebase-database.rules.json`
(change both together).

## Quick start (multiplayer server)

You need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) 20 or newer.

```bash
cd steal-a-monster
npm install
npm start
```

Open **http://localhost:3000**, type a name, pick an outfit colour and press
**PLAY**. New players start with **1,000 Money**, a Wooden Sword, a Boing Glove,
two Sticky Traps and a base tower with room for 15 monsters. A short quest on the left
teaches the loop.

**Play with friends on the same Wi-Fi:** the terminal prints an address like
`http://192.168.1.20:3000` — open it on the other computers/phones.

**Several players on one computer:** open the game in a normal window *and* in
a private/incognito window (or another browser). Each browser profile keeps its
own player token, so each window is a different player. (Two tabs of the same
browser profile are the *same* player — the newest tab takes over.)

`npm run dev` restarts the server when server files change. The **Monster
Gallery** (`/gallery.html`, also linked on the title screen) shows every species
animated side by side.

---

## How to play

| Desktop | Action |
|---|---|
| **W A S D** / ↑ ↓ | Move (camera-relative); walking forward swings the camera behind you |
| **Drag** with the mouse (left or right button) · **← →** | Turn the camera · **V** toggles mouse-look (pointer lock) |
| Mouse wheel | Zoom |
| **Left click** (or **F**) | Swing your sword — it auto-aims at the nearest monster in front of you |
| **Space** | Jump / swim up · **Shift** run |
| **Q** | Dodge roll (brief invulnerability — dodge the red warning areas) |
| **E** | Interact: shops, Lucky Blocks, hold to steal, rescue a dropped monster |
| **R** | Recruit the defeated monster on your newest card (pays its fee) |
| **H** | Teleport to your base (20 s cooldown, not while carrying a stolen monster). Your base has a light beam and a "🏠 YOUR BASE" sign; when you're away, an on-screen 🏠 pointer shows the way and the distance |
| **L** | Switch on your base's security lasers (you must be at your base) |
| **X** | Call your companion monsters (up to 5) to your side |
| **Z** | Your costume's **master power** (Black Spy: 583 damage, Legend Master: 1,200, +130 per power upgrade) |
| **1 – 8** | Use gadgets |
| **C** / Tab · **M** | Your monsters · World map |
| **T** / Enter | Chat · **Esc** close panels / settings · **F3** debug overlay |

**Phones and tablets:** joystick on the left, drag on the right half to look,
big ⚔ attack button, jump, dodge, **E** and 💥 power buttons; 🏠 home, 🔒 lasers
and 🐾 call-your-team at the top; tap the hotbar for gadgets. Settings → *Touch controls* can force them on/off.

### The loop

1. **Explore.** The world is a ring of regions around the starter hub. The
   plaza in the middle has the **Sword Shop**, the **Gadget Shop**, the
   **Costume Shop**, **Upgrade your power**, the **Lucky Board**, the
   **Island Gate** to the seven monster islands and the portals to the
   expansion islands. The 12 player bases ring the plaza. Every region (island)
   holds **50 wild monsters** while someone is on it — 408 species in all,
   each with its own 3D model.
2. **Battle.** Monsters roam their home territories. Some are shy and run, some
   ignore you until hit, territorial ones defend their home, aggressive ones
   chase you. Attacks are telegraphed with red areas on the ground.
3. **Defeat ≠ ownership.** A defeated monster sits dazed for 35 s and everyone
   who helped defeat it gets a **recruitment card** with its stats, perk, income
   and **fee**. The top fighter gets 12 s of priority. Pay the fee (R) to recruit
   it and watch the **capture**: a ring of light lifts it up, it spins into a
   glowing orb, the orb flies to you and it hops out as your new follower.
   If nobody recruits it, it recovers and runs away. A few rare monsters add a
   **condition** shown on the card (for example owning a Tier 7 sword, or
   having discovered 20 species).
4. **Bring it home.** Recruited monsters follow you. Walk into your base (or press
   **H**) and they hop onto free pads automatically (except the ones you chose
   to **bring along** — see *Companions* below). Your base is a block tower:
   every floor has 10 pads, and the floors are joined by **stairs inside the
   tower** (there are no outside stairs, so a thief has to come in through your
   front door and lasers). Rearrange monsters, send one to follow you, or
   release one from the **Monsters** panel.
5. **Earn.** Every monster on a pad earns Money per second (rarer = more) and gives
   a **perk** (more income, speed, XP, max HP, regen, Lucky Block luck, recruit
   discounts, radar range, longer lasers or sword damage). Step on the gold **$**
   pad to collect. While you're offline your base keeps earning at half rate
   (up to 8 hours).
6. **Upgrade.** Better swords (16 swords in 11 tiers, from Wooden to Galaxy, many
   with a special: burn, chain lightning, bubbles that slow, freezing frost, a
   lucky jackpot, a rainbow combo, a star nova… — some need a
   level or a discovered region), more pads (15 → 25 → 35 → 45: each upgrade adds
   10, opening the next floor) and longer-lasting lasers.
   Levels come from XP and unlock new regions. The top swords and upgrades also
   cost **💎 Monster Gems**, the rare material: rare and stronger monsters drop
   them, the Volcanic Kingdom drops extra, **Gem Geodes** in the Volcanic Kingdom
   and Crystal Mountains are full of them, and Lucky Blocks sometimes give some.
7. **Decorate.** Buy decorations at your base (Base panel → Decorations): flower
   beds, lanterns, a bubble fountain, crystal clusters, a golden dragon statue…
   and place them on the 8 spots along your walls. Collection milestones award
   bronze, silver and gold **trophies**. Everyone who visits sees them.
8. **Protect or steal.** Your lasers stay on for 60 s (up to 120 s with
   upgrades), then switch off — come back and re-lock! When a rival's lasers are
   off you can walk in, **hold E** next to a monster and carry it home. Thieves
   are slower and can't teleport. Hit a thief with a gadget and they **drop** the
   monster; its owner can touch it to send it home, otherwise it flies home after
   9 s. If a thief reaches their own base, the monster is theirs.

### The world

| Region | Unlock | Highlights |
|---|---|---|
| Greenstarter Plains | start | Hub, bases, shops, Draklet Hollow (hidden cave), the Elder Oak |
| Deep Jungle | Lv 3 | Giant trees, Crumbite Pond, the hidden Whispering Clearing (night-only Glowmoth) |
| Scorching Desert | Lv 4 | Dunes, Mirage Oasis, the Sunken Chamber (Pharaoling) |
| Sunken Ocean | Lv 5 | Swim between islands, the Old Shipwreck, Coral Cove (Spoutlet) |
| Frozen Highlands | Lv 6 | Slippery Frostglass Lake, Yetibo Cave |
| Shadow Forest | Lv 9 | Glowing mushrooms, Moonlit Hollow (night-only Gloomkit & Nightmaw) |
| Ancient Ruins | Lv 11 | Pressure-plate puzzle that opens the vault of the guardian Titanub |
| Crystal Mountains | Lv 12 | Terraced cliffs, Geode Grotto (Gemhorn), Prism Peak |
| Volcanic Kingdom | Lv 14 | Lava pools (they burn!), the volcano crater lair of Pyrodrake |
| Legendary Wilderness | Lv 20 + Tier 6 sword | Celestail, the Aurora Wyrm nest, a secret glitchy something |
| Bloomveil Isle | 3+ players online, Lv 5 | Expansion island (portal in the plaza) |
| Starfall Isle | 6+ players online, Lv 15 | Expansion island |

There is a day/night cycle (12 minutes); some monsters only come out at night.

### The seven monster islands

Walk up to the golden **Island Gate** in the plaza to travel. Every island has
**50 monsters of its own** — 16 Common, 13 Uncommon, 10 Rare, 6 Epic,
3 Legendary (they live at the island's **lair**) and 2 **Mythic** (at its
**shrine**) — 350 in all, none shared with another island. A portal on each
island brings you back to the plaza.

| Island | Unlock | Levels | Mythic | Legendary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cute Monster Island | Lv 1 | 1–8 | Dreamy Rainbowcorn, Queen Sugarplume | Starlight Chickadee, Captain Cuddlebear, Princess Sparklehog |
| Coral Reef Island | Lv 5 | 5–12 | King Coralcrown, Abyssal Sea Serpent | Admiral Inkwell, Pearl Emperor Crab, Duchess Tidejaw |
| Ember Peak Island | Lv 9 | 9–16 | Volcanus Rex, Infernal Beetle Lord | Magma Monarch, Phoenix Flarefox, Lord Cinderclaw |
| Frostbite Island | Lv 13 | 13–20 | Blizzard Titan, Frostfang the Eternal | Aurora Stag, Snow Empress Wolf, Glacier Guardian Owl |
| Thunder Cloud Island | Lv 17 | 17–24 | Tempest Thunderbird, Zephyr the Storm Lynx | Sky Sovereign Kit, Thunderbeak, Queen Buzzvolt |
| Moonshade Island | Lv 21 | 21–28 | Void Maw, Moonqueen Selenia | Duke Nightshade, Lunar Specter, Count Batula |
| Dragon Crown Island | Lv 25 | 25–34 | Aurelion the Dragon King, Empress Rubyscale | Golden Wyvern, Sapphire Unihorn, Diamond Celestia |

### The moon secret of Cute Monster Island

All 50 monsters on Cute Monster Island are cute — and the island hides a
**Secret** one:

1. Find the **five small round moon buttons** hidden around the island and
   step on them. Each one turns **blue** and the game says *"You found a moon
   button! 1/5"* (2/5, …). The 🌙 counter under the minimap shows your
   progress; it is saved.
2. With all five lit, a **Moon Portal** appears out of nowhere and an arrow on
   screen points the way.
3. The portal takes you to the **Moon Sky Arena**: floating stones under a
   giant moon. Jump from stone to stone to four battle platforms. On each, a
   cute monster appears that only fights you: **Round 1 an Uncommon, Round 2 a
   Rare, Round 3 an Epic, Round 4 a Legendary.** Fall off and you are put back
   on the last platform you reached.
4. Win round 4 and the **Secret Lunamochi** (a moon mochi bunny) goes straight
   to your base. Clearing the arena again pays 25,000 Money and 12 💎 instead.

### Companions

Open a monster in **Monsters** and press **🐾 Bring along** — up to **five**
can walk with you. They follow in a little formation and **fight with you**:
when a wild monster attacks you, when you hit one, or when one comes for you,
your team runs over and attacks it (their damage counts as yours, so you can
recruit it afterwards). If one ends up more than about **9 feet** (7.5 m) away
while not fighting, it pops back to your side; press **X** to call the whole
team at once. Companions can't be hurt, never fight other players, and stay
with you when you go home (a monster you just recruited still moves into your
base). Everyone sees your team.

### Costumes and master powers

The **Costume Shop** in the plaza sells costumes. A costume changes your look
and gives you its own **idle, attack, dodge and teleport animations** and a
**master power** on **Z** (exact damage, ignores defence):

| Costume | Price | Power (Z) |
|---|---|---|
| 🕶️ **Black Spy** — all black: jacket with the game logo, hat, shoes and gloves. **At night** glowing stickman lines follow your bones and LED lights blink on the suit. Comes with the **Spy Sword** (Tier 9, 200 damage, 20% critical hits). | 150,000 | **Master Power**: a slash wave in front of you, **583** damage to up to 6 monsters, 6 s |
| 🔥 Flame Ninja | 60,000 | Inferno Burst: ring of fire, 320 + burning, 5 s |
| ❄️ Frost Knight | 45,000 | Blizzard Nova: 260 to everything around you and freezes them, 5.5 s |
| ⚡ Thunder Hero | 90,000 | Thunder Strike: 420, lightning that jumps between 3 monsters, 5.5 s |
| 🐰 Bunny Hoodie | 25,000 | Sweet Hug: 180 around you and heals you 40%, 7 s |
| 👑 **Legend Master** — glowing armour, a crown, a long cape, glowing lines and three orbs circling you. **Choose its power** right after buying it. | **11,000,000** | Depends on the power, **1,200** damage, 6 s (see below) |

**Legend Master.** Right after you buy it a **"Choose your power"** window
opens (change it later with *Change power* in the Costume Shop). The power
decides the costume's **colours**, its glow and aura, its animations, the
effects of its sword moves and its master power:

| Power | Master power (Z) |
|---|---|
| 🔥 Fire | Phoenix Inferno: a ring of fire with pillars of flame, sets everything on fire (12 m) |
| ❄️ Ice | Absolute Zero: two rings of ice spikes burst out of the ground and freeze everything (13 m) |
| ⚡ Lightning | Thunder God: lightning from the sky on up to 6 monsters |
| 🌑 Shadow | Void Eclipse: a huge wave of darkness in front of you (18 m, 180°) |
| ☀️ Light | Holy Judgment: pillars of light around you; heals you 30% |
| 🌌 Cosmic | Galaxy Collapse: a star explosion, the widest ring (15 m) |

The power animation charges up (you rise, the orbs speed up), then releases
with a screen flash and camera shake. The Legend Master also has **10
different sword moves** that come one after the other — attack 1 uses move 1,
attack 2 uses move 2 … attack 10 uses move 10, then it starts again: Crescent
Slash, Return Slash, Sky Splitter, Rising Dragon, Cyclone Cut, Piercing Light,
Cross Strike, Meteor Drop, Whirlwind and Legend Break, each with its own
glowing slash in the power's colours. Everyone sees the same move (the server
counts them).

Next door, **Upgrade your power** adds **+130** damage to every costume power
per level (10 levels; 20,000, 40,000, 60,000 … Money), so the Black Spy's
Master Power goes 583 → 713 → 843 …
Entering a landmark or hidden place for the first time is a **discovery** with
a Money reward; the **Monsterdex** tracks every species you have met.

### Base guards

In the **🏠 My Base** panel (at your base) you can hire **guards** for
**420,000,000**: 2 guards with swords. They attack anyone who walks into your
base, anyone carrying one of your monsters nearby, and anyone who hits them —
never you. They **can be beaten**: a knocked-out guard gets up again after
90 s. Each **upgrade** (60,000,000 × the current level) brings more guards,
better uniforms and swords, and stricter facilities:

| Level | Guards | Uniform / sword | Facilities |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1–2 | 2 / 4 | blue cap / stone, iron | "GUARDED" sign |
| 3–4 | 6 / 8 | police / iron, steel | + guard booth |
| 5–6 | 10 / 12 | armour / steel, flame | + barrier |
| 7–8 | 15 / 18 | black elite with red visor / thunder | + helipad, 1 / 2 **helicopters with guns** |
| 9 | 21 | black elite / celestial | + searchlights, 3 helicopters |
| **10** | **24** | **gold armour, red cape / Galaxy Sword** (140 damage) | **4 helicopters** |

Helicopters circle the tower and shoot thieves near it while at least one
guard is standing. When a thief comes in, the owner sees **"🚨 THIEF! … is
trying to steal your monsters — your guards are fighting!"** at the top of the
screen and everyone sees a blinking **🦹 THIEF!** tag over the thief. When the
thief knocks out every guard, the owner sees **"💥 The thief … has defeated
your guards!"**.

### Lucky Blocks and LUCKY LUCKY

Golden **?** blocks sit around every region — walk up and swing at one (or press
E). Rewards are rolled on the server: Money, XP, gadgets, new swords, hats,
recruit coupons, **clues** that reveal a rare monster on your map, or a surprise
**encounter** (still has to be defeated and paid for).

Every ~14 minutes the global **LUCKY LUCKY** event starts after a 10-second
countdown: the sky turns gold and rainbow, dozens of Lucky Blocks appear near
players, rare monsters spawn 3× as often and the event-only **Luckitty** roams.

### Gadgets (multiplayer items)

Boing Glove (knockback), Sticky Trap, Freeze Ray, Tangle Net, Slippery Gel,
Bubble Shield, Zoom Soda (speed) and Monster Radar. Gadgets only affect
players, have ranges and cooldowns checked by the server, and any hit on a thief
makes them drop the stolen monster.

## Multiplayer and deployment

`npm start` runs the web server **and** the real-time game server on one port.
Every important rule runs on the server. (The static web build is different:
it runs the same server code inside the browser, see above.)

| Environment variable | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `PORT` | Port to listen on | `3000` |
| `HOST` | Interface to bind | `0.0.0.0` |
| `DATA_DIR` | Where player saves go | `./data` |
| `MAX_PLAYERS` | Players per server (max 12 = number of base plots) | `12` |
| `EXPANSION_THRESHOLDS` | Players needed to open Bloomveil,Starfall | `3,6` |
| `LUCKY_EVENT_FIRST_MS` / `LUCKY_EVENT_INTERVAL_MS` | LUCKY LUCKY timing | 4 min / 14 min |
| `DEV_COMMANDS=1` | Enables `/lucky`, `/money N`, `/level N`, `/night`, `/day`, `/spawn <species>`, `/tp X Z` in chat | off |
| `NODE_ENV=production` | Longer browser caching | |

Example: `PORT=8080 DATA_DIR=/var/lib/steal-a-monster NODE_ENV=production npm start`.
On Windows PowerShell: `$env:PORT=8080; npm start`.

**Over the internet:**

- **A VPS / your own machine:** run `npm start` behind a reverse proxy (nginx,
  Caddy) that forwards WebSockets, or forward the port on your router. If the
  page is served over `https://`, Socket.IO automatically uses `wss://` on the
  same host.
- **Render, Railway, Fly.io and similar:** create a Node service in the
  `steal-a-monster` folder with build command `npm ci` and start command
  `npm start`. Use **one instance** (the game state lives in that process) and
  attach a persistent disk/volume mounted at `DATA_DIR`, otherwise saves are lost
  on every deploy.
- `GET /health` returns player/monster counts and save-failure counters for
  monitoring.

Stopping the server with Ctrl+C (SIGINT/SIGTERM) saves every online player first.

### Server authority

Clients send **intentions** ("I moved here", "I swung facing this way",
"recruit monster 42", "use gadget X facing Y"). The server owns positions of
monsters, all health values, damage rolls, cooldowns, Money, inventories,
ownership, base locks and events.

- **Movement** is predicted on the client for responsiveness and **validated**
  on the server: maximum speed (with tolerance for lag and knockback), height
  above ground, walls (a move through a base tower wall, a shop or a cave wall
  is refused, so the upper floors of a base can only be reached by its inside
  stairs), the world edge, locked regions, closed expansion islands, other
  players' locked bases and the sealed ruins vault. Invalid moves are snapped back.
  Teleports (H, portals, respawn) only go to server-chosen destinations and carry
  a sequence number so late packets can't undo them.
- **Combat:** the server picks targets from its own positions, applies sword
  range/arc/cooldown/max targets, rolls crits and specials, and broadcasts results.
- **Transactions** (recruit, purchases, upgrades) are synchronous on the server,
  carry a client request id and are answered from a cache on retry, so a network
  hiccup can never charge twice or grant twice.
- Every message is schema-checked and rate-limited; unknown messages are ignored;
  the client can't name prices, damage, rewards or coordinates.

### Persistence

Each player has a **versioned JSON profile** (`schemaVersion: 2`; older saves are
migrated on load — version 2 added Monster Gems and decorations) named after a
hash of a random secret token kept in the browser's localStorage (the token
itself is never stored on the server). Saves are written atomically (temp file →
fsync → keep previous as `.bak` → rename); a corrupt file falls back to the
backup, and if both are unreadable the login is **refused** instead of creating
a fresh profile. Profiles are saved every 5 s when changed and immediately after
any Money/ownership transaction; failed saves are retried. Loaded data is
sanitised (unknown species/swords/items dropped, duplicate ids and doubled pads
fixed, Money and Gems clamped, never more decorations placed than owned).

Accounts (`accounts.json`, scrypt password hashes and "remember me" key
hashes) and bans (`bans.json`) are stored next to the profiles. An account's
profile id is derived from the account, not from the browser token, so logging
in on another device opens the same profile. Online (Firebase) accounts keep
their profile in the database instead; the room's game treats that profile as
the truth when the player joins and writes it back every 10 s.

An **ownership ledger** (`data/ownership.json`, written before profiles on every
transfer) is the source of truth for who owns which monster, so a crash between
two profile writes during a theft can neither duplicate nor lose a monster.

> **Development storage.** The JSON store is meant for a single server process
> and moderate player counts. It is not a database: no multi-server access, no
> transactions spanning files, and the whole ledger is rewritten on change. For a
> real deployment implement the four methods of the store interface
> (`loadProfile`, `saveProfile`, `loadLedger`, `saveLedger` in
> `server/storage.js`) on PostgreSQL/SQLite/Redis — e.g. one row per player plus a
> `monster_owner` table updated in the same transaction as both profiles.

### Extending the game

- **A new monster:** add an entry to `SPECIES` in `shared/monsters.js` — stats,
  temperament, attacks (melee / lunge / projectile / slam / breath), perk, spawn
  rules (regions + weight, or a hidden `spot`, `time: 'night'`, events) and a model
  recipe (body shape, head, eyes/mouth styles, ears, horns, crest, wings, tail,
  legs, arms, back decorations, extras, aura). Check it at `/gallery.html?only=<id>`.
  Combat, AI, recruitment, bases, UI and tests pick it up automatically.
- **Swords / gadgets / Lucky rewards / cosmetics:** `shared/weapons.js`,
  `shared/items.js`, `shared/lucky.js`.
- **A region:** add it to `REGIONS` (shape, levels, unlock, `minPopulation`,
  terrain style, colours, props) and optional spots in `shared/world.js`; every
  region gets `CONFIG.monsters.perRegion` wild monsters.
- **An event:** add a definition to `EVENT_DEFS` in `server/services/events.js`
  (`onStart`, `onEnd`, `spawnTick`); the lifecycle and client sync are generic.
- **Balance:** `shared/config.js`.

### Assets

There are **no external asset files**. Monsters, players, swords, hats, props,
terrain, sky and particles are generated in code; sounds are synthesised with the
Web Audio API (`public/client/audio.js`). To use recorded sounds, call
`audio.setSample('<name>', url)` with the same names the game already plays
(`hit`, `coin`, `recruit`, `alarm`, ...). Hand-made glTF models could replace
`buildMonster()` per species, as long as they expose the same rig pivots
(`head`, `eyes`, `tail`, `legs`, ...) the animation system drives.

## Testing

```bash
npm test            # automated: node --test, 85 tests, runs in CI
npm run test:e2e    # two real browsers on one server (needs Playwright + Chromium)
npm run test:load   # 12 simulated players; reports server tick time and bandwidth
```

The automated suites run the real server code (with a controllable clock and an
in-memory or temporary-directory store) and, for networking, a real HTTP +
Socket.IO server with real socket clients. Requirement → test:

| # | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | New player gets exactly 1,000 Money | `profile.test.js` |
| 2 | Reconnect/refresh/respawn gives no second bonus | `profile.test.js` |
| 3, 4 | Two clients on one server, different bases, see each other move | `multiplayer.test.js` |
| 5 | Monsters have distinct real 3D models and working health | `combat.test.js` (builds all 408 models in Node) |
| 6 | Sword attacks apply valid damage (reach, facing, cooldown, no client damage) | `combat.test.js` |
| 7 | Monsters attack and can knock out players; respawn at own base | `combat.test.js` |
| 8 | Defeated monsters enter the recruitment state | `combat.test.js` |
| 9, 10, 11 | Recruit fails without Money / deducts exact price / never twice | `recruitment.test.js` |
| 12 | Placing on a free pad, one pad per monster | `recruitment.test.js` |
| 13 | Passive income rules, collecting, offline cap | `recruitment.test.js` |
| 14, 15 | Lasers block entry and theft / disabled lasers allow theft and transfer once | `stealing.test.js` |
| 16 | Interrupting a thief releases the monster (both drop rules) | `stealing.test.js` |
| 17 | H only to own base, cooldown, not while carrying | `stealing.test.js` |
| 18 | Gadget distance, facing, cooldown, shields, consumables | `stealing.test.js` |
| 19 | Lucky Blocks can't pay out twice | `world.test.js` |
| 20 | LUCKY LUCKY lifecycle and synchronisation between players | `world.test.js`, `multiplayer.test.js` |
| 21 | Regions open/close at population thresholds | `world.test.js` |
| 22 | Forged requests can't create Money/ownership/teleports | `world.test.js`, `multiplayer.test.js` |
| 23 | Progress survives a server restart (file storage) | `profile.test.js` |
| 24 | Disconnects during recruitment or theft keep ownership consistent | `recruitment.test.js`, `stealing.test.js` |
| — | Seven islands × 50 species, Island Gate, lairs and shrines | `islands.test.js` |
| — | Moon buttons, portal, arena rounds, the secret monster | `moon.test.js` |
| — | Five companions follow, pop back, defend you, X calls them | `companions.test.js` |
| — | Costumes, Spy Sword, 583 master power, +130 power upgrades | `costumes.test.js` |
| — | Legend Master: 11,000,000, choose a power, 1,200 damage, 10 sword moves in a row | `costumes.test.js` |
| — | Accounts, unique names, start over / continue, admins Daniel, Nadine, Prabu and Shallom (Player list, return, ban) | `accounts.test.js` |
| — | Guards: 420,000,000, upgrades to 24 guards + 4 helicopters, thief alerts, can be beaten | `guards.test.js` |

See **[TESTING.md](TESTING.md)** for what was verified by hand in a browser and
what remains unverified.

---

## Status and known limitations

The full loop is playable end to end in the browser and covered by automated
tests (see [TESTING.md](TESTING.md) for exactly what was and wasn't verified).
Known limitations:

- **Not verified on real hardware**: no real GPU, phone, Safari or Firefox was
  available while building this; frame rates on real devices are unmeasured.
- **Bases** are 5-floor towers with upgradeable pads (up to 45), lasers at the
  ground-floor door, income, a collector and 8 fixed ground-floor decoration
  spots; decorations can't be placed anywhere else, and they have no
  collision (you walk through them).
- **Movement** is predicted by the client and validated by the server (speed,
  terrain, walls, region locks, lasers); the server does not re-simulate every
  step. A cheater cannot teleport, pass walls or locked lasers, or create Money
  or monsters, but could move optimally within the speed limit.
- **Storage** is one JSON file per player (atomic writes + backups) in a single
  server process. That suits one world on one machine; a bigger deployment
  would swap in a database behind the same store interface.
- **Audio** is synthesized sound effects only (no recorded sounds or music).
- **Art** is entirely procedural (no imported models or textures).
- **Balance** (prices, income, spawn rates) has not been tuned by long playtests.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Cannot reach the game server"** — start it with `npm start` and open the
  address it prints (not the HTML file directly).
- **Black screen / very slow** — the game needs WebGL 2. Lower *Graphics* in
  Settings (Low disables shadows and shortens the view distance; it applies
  immediately, antialiasing after a reload). Press **F3** to see FPS and draw calls.
- **"Your saved progress could not be loaded"** — the profile file and its backup
  are both unreadable; nothing was overwritten. Look in `DATA_DIR/players/`.
- **Camera doesn't turn** — drag with the mouse, use the ← → keys, or press V
  (some embedded browsers block pointer lock).
- **Port in use** — `PORT=3001 npm start`.

# Testing STEAL A MONSTER

This file separates what was **tested automatically**, what was **checked in a
real browser** (scripted or by looking at it), and what is **not verified**.

Test environment: Node.js 22 (unit tests also on Node 20.20), headless Chromium
via Playwright with **SwiftShader software WebGL** on a 4-core Linux container.
There was no real GPU, phone, Safari or Firefox available.


Socket.IO server with real socket clients.

These need Playwright and Chromium (`npm i -D playwright` or a global install).
They are not part of CI because they take minutes and need a browser.

### Two-player end-to-end test — `npm run test:e2e`

Starts its own server and drives **two real browser pages** (Alice and Bob)
with the real controls (keys, camera, pointer). The result of the last run:

```
Alice joins
  ✔ new player starts with 1,000 Money (got 1000)
Alice walks out and fights
  ✔ a Chompkin is visible on the client
  ✔ Alice defeated it with her sword (state 7)
  ✔ a recruitment card appeared

Alice pays to recruit (R)
  ✔ Alice now owns the Chompkin
  ✔ the fee was paid (1011 -> 891)
Alice presses H and her monster moves in
  ✔ teleported home
  ✔ monster placed on pad 0
Bob joins and steals it
  ✔ Bob has his own base (#2) and 1,000 Money
  ✔ Bob is carrying the stolen monster
  ✔ Alice sees the theft alert
  ✔ still owned by Alice while it is being carried
  ✔ Bob delivered it: ownership transferred
  ✔ Alice lost it (exactly one owner)
Bob locks his base; Alice cannot get in
  ✔ Alice's client shows Bob's lasers switched on
  ✔ the laser gate stopped Alice at the door
  ✔ the server agrees: Alice is not inside
LUCKY LUCKY: Alice opens a Lucky Block
  ✔ the event started and Lucky Blocks appeared on the client
  ✔ Alice opened a Lucky Block (1)

  ✔ Bob: no browser errors 
client (software rendering, 2 browsers on one CPU): fps 3, game logic 2.1 ms/frame, render 10.7 ms/frame, 411 draw calls, 238580 triangles

E2E PASSED
```

Because SwiftShader renders at about 1–2 frames per second with two browsers on
one CPU, the bots pause drawing (`__app.skipRender`) while they walk and fight so
they move in real time; game logic, input and networking keep running, and
drawing is switched back on before every check that looks at the screen.

`node scripts/build-web.mjs` builds a static site in `dist-web/`. It was served
from a sub-folder by a plain static file server (like GitHub Pages) and played
in headless Chromium: the title says single-player, a new player gets 1,000
Money, a Chompkin was fought, defeated and recruited with R, H took the player
home, and after a page reload the monster and Money were still there (no second
starting bonus, no income jackpot). No browser errors, no failed requests.

### Server load test — `npm run test:load`

12 simulated players (real Socket.IO clients, the server's player cap) walk out
of their tower bases through the door, round the towers into the plains and
swing swords for 60 s while the server ticks are timed. The bots slide around
trees and walls like the real client, and the server refused none of their
moves (0 corrections). On this 4-core container the 20 Hz tick used about
1.5 ms of its 50 ms budget at the 95th percentile, and each client received
about 20 KB/s (the event-loop lag figures are at the monitor's 10 ms resolution):

```

  "players": 12,
  "seconds": 60,
  "monsters": 135,
  "ticks": 1198,

  "budgetMs": 50,
  "eventLoopLagMs": { "p50": 10.2, "p99": 11.6 },
  "downKBps": { "avg": 20.3, "max": 22.6 },
  "corrections": 0,
  "rssMB": 111
}

LOAD OK: p95 tick 1.53 ms of a 50 ms budget
```

All 12 bots stay in the plains here (new players can't enter the other regions
yet), so the plains has its 50 monsters and the regions next to it 20 each.

### Worst-case monster population — `npm run bench:population`

12 players, each on a different region/island, so 12 regions fill to 50
monsters at once (605 wild monsters). The real `Game` runs in-process with a
simulated clock; every tick (AI, attacks, snapshots for all 12 players) is
timed after the regions have filled:

```
monsters: 605 (50 or 51 in each of the 12 regions; the extra one is a hidden-spot monster)
tickMs:   avg 0.47, p50 0.51, p95 0.88, p99 1.39, max 4.78  (budget 50)
download: about 26 KB/s per player (max 33.5)
```

The players in this benchmark walk slowly and don't fight, so it measures the
cost of the population itself; a client only receives the monsters within
135 m of it.

Opens every panel (Monsters, Dex, sword shop, gadget shop, Base, Lucky board,

(layout, text fitting, 3D previews rendering).

### Rendering cost (software rendering, so frame rate is not meaningful)

Measured with `renderer.info` at four places in the world after the
performance pass (far-plane culling, chunked props with detail culling, merged
monster meshes with a low-poly copy for far-away monsters, instanced base pads
and clouds, distance-culled labels):

| Quality | Draw calls | Triangles |
|---|---|---|
| Low | 250–420 | 160–215 K |
| High (incl. shadow pass) | 470–630 | 230–320 K |

Before the pass: 430–980 draw calls and 430–830 K triangles at Low.

With **50 wild monsters on every island** the client receives 45–60 monsters
at a time. Far-away monsters are not drawn (Low: beyond 80 m, Medium: 110 m,
High: 150 m; one that is chasing you is always drawn). Measured in the
single-player build after the islands filled up, in the plains meadow and the
jungle: Low 160–260 draw calls, 170–205 K triangles; High 690–750 draw calls,
330 K triangles. Without the distance limit Low was 470–540 draw calls.
Press **F3** in the game to see these numbers live.

Lucky Blocks, Gem Geodes and glowing swords used to carry their own point
light. In three.js every extra light makes all lit materials more expensive
and recompiles their shaders whenever the light count changes, so the LUCKY
LUCKY event (two dozen blocks) was very slow. They now use an additive glow
sprite instead; in the two-browser e2e run the CPU time spent submitting a
frame during the event dropped from about 300 ms to about 11 ms.

## 4. Not verified

- **Real-GPU frame rate.** No hardware GPU was available. Draw-call and
  triangle counts are reasonable for WebGL, but the actual FPS on desktop,
  laptop or phone hardware was never measured.
- **Real phones and tablets.** Touch controls were tested only with Chromium's
  mobile emulation (joystick, buttons, layout), not on an actual device.
- **Safari and Firefox.** Only Chromium was tested.
- **Internet conditions.** All multiplayer tests ran on localhost; latency,
  jitter and packet loss over a real network were not tested (the client
  interpolates with a 120 ms buffer and the server tolerates jitter in its
  movement checks, but that is untested in the wild).
- **Long sessions.** No multi-hour server run or memory-growth test.
- **Audio.** Sounds are synthesized with Web Audio and play without errors,
  but were not listened to by a person.
- **Game balance.** Prices, income, spawn rates and difficulty were set by
  reasoning, not by playtesting over hours.
- **Multiple server processes.** The game is designed for one Node process
  per world; horizontal scaling is not supported or tested.

# Panduan: main online bareng teman dengan Firebase

Panduan ini membuat tombol **🌐 Play online with friends** di game kamu
(https://kenshirodaniel8-bit.github.io/minecraft-realistis/) bisa dipakai.
Kamu cukup melakukannya **satu kali**. Gratis, tanpa kartu kredit.

> ### ⚡ Yang perlu kamu lakukan SEKARANG (versi dengan akun)
>
> Config Firebase kamu (`steal-a-monster`) **sudah terpasang** di game, jadi
> Langkah 4 dan 5 sudah selesai. Karena sekarang game memakai **akun**, masih
> ada 3 hal yang harus kamu lakukan sendiri di Firebase Console:
>
> 1. **Langkah 3** — tempel dan **Publish** aturan (Rules) yang **baru** dari
>    `firebase-database.rules.json`. Aturan lama tidak mengizinkan akun, jadi
>    tanpa ini login/simpan progres akan ditolak (*permission denied*).
> 2. **Langkah 3b** — nyalakan login **Email/Password** di *Authentication*.
> 3. **Langsung buat akun admin** di game: **Daniel**, **Nadine** (akun `naddd`), **Prabu**
>    dan **Shallom** (lihat bagian *Akun dan admin*). Siapa pun yang pertama
>    membuat akun dengan nama itu menjadi admin semua server, jadi jangan
>    sampai keduluan orang lain.
>
> Kalau sebelum ini kamu sudah mencoba *Create account* dan gagal, tidak
> apa-apa: setelah langkah 1 dan 2 selesai, coba **Create account** lagi
> dengan nama dan password yang sama.

## Cara kerjanya (singkat)

- Satu pemain menekan **Create room**. Browser dia menjalankan "server" game,
  sama seperti waktu main sendiri.
- Dia mengirim **link room** (atau kode 5 huruf, misalnya `K7QZP`) ke teman.
- Teman membuka link lalu menekan **Join**. Semua pesan game (gerak, serang,
  rekrut, curi, dan lain-lain) lewat **Firebase Realtime Database**, sebuah
  database online gratis milik Google.
- Aturannya tetap sama: hanya game si pembuat room yang memutuskan uang,
  monster, dan pemiliknya. Teman cuma mengirim "aku bergerak / aku menyerang".

---

## Langkah 1: Buat project Firebase

1. Buka **https://console.firebase.google.com** lalu login dengan akun Google.
2. Klik **Create a project** (atau **Add project**).
3. Nama project: misalnya `steal-a-monster`, lalu klik **Continue**.
4. Google Analytics tidak perlu, jadi matikan saja. Klik **Create project**,
   tunggu sebentar, lalu klik **Continue**.

## Langkah 2: Buat Realtime Database

1. Di menu kiri pilih **Build → Realtime Database**.
2. Klik **Create Database**.
3. Lokasi: pilih **Singapore (asia-southeast1)**, yang paling dekat ke
   Indonesia sehingga lag-nya paling kecil. Klik **Next**.
4. Pilih **Start in locked mode**, lalu klik **Enable**.
5. Di bagian atas halaman data ada alamat database, contohnya
   `https://steal-a-monster-12345-default-rtdb.asia-southeast1.firebasedatabase.app`.
   Alamat ini dipakai di Langkah 4.

## Langkah 3: Pasang aturan keamanan (Rules)

1. Masih di Realtime Database, buka tab **Rules**.
2. Hapus semua tulisan yang ada.
3. Salin seluruh isi file
   [`firebase-database.rules.json`](firebase-database.rules.json) (ada di
   folder `steal-a-monster`), lalu tempel di sana.
4. Klik **Publish**.

Aturan ini mengatur:

- **Akun** (`sam/accounts/...`): hanya pemilik akun yang bisa menulis
  akunnya sendiri, dan nama di akun harus sama dengan nama yang dipakai
  untuk login (jadi tidak ada yang bisa menyamar jadi admin).
- **Ban dan pengembalian monster** (`sam/bans`, `sam/returns`): hanya akun
  admin (Daniel, Nadine, Prabu, Shallom) yang bisa menulisnya.
- **Room** (`sam/rooms/KODE`): harus login; pemain yang di-ban tidak bisa
  membuat atau masuk room; tidak ada yang bisa mengirim pesan atas nama orang
  lain; hanya pembuat room yang bisa menutupnya. Daftar room tidak bisa dibaca.

Kalau nanti file `firebase-database.rules.json` berubah lagi (misalnya setelah
update game), ulangi langkah ini supaya aturan di Firebase ikut baru.

## Langkah 3b: Nyalakan login akun (Authentication)

Akun pemain memakai **Firebase Authentication**. Pemain tidak perlu punya
email: game membuat "email" sendiri dari nama, misalnya nama `Mira Fox`
menjadi `mira.fox@players.steal-a-monster.game`. Pemain cukup mengisi **nama**
dan **password** (minimal 6 karakter).

1. Di menu kiri pilih **Build → Authentication**.
2. Klik **Get started**. **Wajib** kalau tombol ini muncul: tanpa ini semua
   pendaftaran ditolak (error `CONFIGURATION_NOT_FOUND`).
3. Buka tab **Sign-in method**.
4. Di daftar *Native providers* pilih **Email/Password**.
5. Nyalakan tombol **Enable** yang pertama (Email/Password). Yang kedua,
   *Email link (passwordless sign-in)*, **biarkan mati**.
6. Klik **Save**.

> **Jangan menambah pemain lewat tombol *Add user* di Firebase Console**
> (misalnya dengan email Gmail). Akun game dibuat **di dalam game** lewat
> **Create account** dengan nama game (misalnya `Daniel`). Di tab *Users*
> akun itu akan muncul sebagai `daniel@players.steal-a-monster.game`. User
> yang ditambah dengan email biasa bukan akun game dan tidak bisa dipakai
> login di game (boleh dihapus).

Selesai. Kalau langkah ini terlewat, pemain akan melihat tulisan
*"Accounts are not switched on yet…"* saat mencoba membuat akun.

## Langkah 4: Daftarkan aplikasi web dan salin config

1. Klik ikon **⚙ (gerigi)** di sebelah *Project Overview*, lalu pilih
   **Project settings**.
2. Di tab **General**, gulir ke bawah sampai bagian **Your apps**, lalu klik
   ikon **`</>`** (Web).
3. Nama aplikasi: misalnya `steal-a-monster-web`. Jangan centang *Firebase
   Hosting*. Klik **Register app**.
4. Akan muncul kode seperti ini. Salin bagian `{ ... }`-nya:

   ```js
   const firebaseConfig = {
     apiKey: "AIzaSyB...",
     authDomain: "steal-a-monster-12345.firebaseapp.com",
     databaseURL: "https://steal-a-monster-12345-default-rtdb.asia-southeast1.firebasedatabase.app",
     projectId: "steal-a-monster-12345",
     storageBucket: "steal-a-monster-12345.appspot.com",
     messagingSenderId: "123456789012",
     appId: "1:123456789012:web:abcdef123456"
   };
   ```

5. **Penting:** pastikan ada baris `databaseURL`. Kalau tidak ada, tambahkan
   sendiri dengan alamat dari Langkah 2 nomor 5.

> `apiKey` Firebase **bukan rahasia**. Kunci ini memang selalu ada di halaman
> web, jadi aman ditaruh di GitHub. Yang menjaga database adalah Rules dari
> Langkah 3.

## Langkah 5: Tempel config ke game (lewat GitHub)

1. Buka **https://github.com/kenshirodaniel8-bit/minecraft-realistis**.
2. Di kiri atas, pilih branch **`claude/steal-a-monster-game-mjo51w`**. Itu
   branch yang dipakai untuk website game. Kalau nanti sudah di-merge ke
   `main`, edit di `main`.
3. Buka file **`steal-a-monster/public/firebase-config.js`**.
4. Klik ikon **✏ (Edit this file)**.
5. Ganti baris paling bawah

   ```js
   export const FIREBASE_CONFIG = null;
   ```

   dengan config kamu (perhatikan `export const FIREBASE_CONFIG =` di depan):

   ```js
   export const FIREBASE_CONFIG = {
     apiKey: "AIzaSyB...",
     authDomain: "steal-a-monster-12345.firebaseapp.com",
     databaseURL: "https://steal-a-monster-12345-default-rtdb.asia-southeast1.firebasedatabase.app",
     projectId: "steal-a-monster-12345",
     storageBucket: "steal-a-monster-12345.appspot.com",
     messagingSenderId: "123456789012",
     appId: "1:123456789012:web:abcdef123456"
   };
   ```

6. Klik **Commit changes…**, lalu **Commit changes** lagi.
7. Buka tab **Actions**. Workflow **Publish Steal a Monster** akan berjalan
   sendiri (2–4 menit). Tunggu sampai tanda centangnya **hijau ✓**.

## Langkah 6: Main bareng!

1. Buka **https://kenshirodaniel8-bit.github.io/minecraft-realistis/**.
   Kalau sebelumnya sudah dibuka, tekan **Ctrl + F5** (atau tarik layar ke
   bawah di HP) supaya versi barunya termuat.
2. **Kamu (pembuat room):** pilih **Create account** (pertama kali) atau
   **Log in**, isi nama dan password, lalu tekan **Create room**. Muncul
   pertanyaan *"start over from the beginning, or continue?"*: pilih
   **Continue** untuk melanjutkan progres, atau **Start over** untuk mulai
   dari nol (progres akun benar-benar dihapus).
3. Di atas layar muncul tombol **🌐 Room K7QZP · 1 player · 🔗 Copy link**.
   Tekan tombol itu supaya link tersalin, lalu kirim ke teman (WhatsApp,
   Discord, dll).
4. **Teman:** buka link itu, buat akun atau login, lalu tekan **Join**. Kode
   room sudah terisi otomatis. Bisa juga dengan mengetik kode 5 hurufnya
   sendiri.
5. Satu room bisa diisi sampai **12 pemain** (ada 12 base).

---

## Akun dan admin

- **Nama tidak boleh sama.** "Mira Fox", "mira fox" dan "Mira   Fox"
  dianggap nama yang sama. Spasi boleh. Nama 2–16 huruf/angka/spasi/`_`/`-`.
- **Monster ikut ke mana saja.** Progres (monster, uang, kostum, penjaga, dan
  lain-lain) disimpan di **akun masing-masing pemain** di Firebase. Monster
  yang kamu dapat di room teman tetap ada di game kamu sendiri dan di room
  lain. Progres disimpan otomatis kira-kira setiap 10 detik.
- **Main tanpa akun** tetap bisa untuk main sendiri (progres disimpan di
  browser itu saja). Untuk main online harus login.
- **Admin:** akun bernama **Daniel**, **Nadine** (akun `naddd`), **Prabu** dan **Shallom**
  adalah admin di **semua** room (huruf besar/kecil tidak berpengaruh). Hanya
  admin yang punya tombol **🛡 Player**, dan admin tidak bisa mem-ban admin
  lain. Di situ muncul semua pemain di
  room itu, monster apa yang sudah mereka curi dan dari siapa, dengan tombol:
  - **↩ Return to …** — monster curian dikembalikan ke pemiliknya (langsung
    masuk base kalau pemiliknya sedang online; kalau tidak, monsternya
    menunggu di akun pemilik dan datang saat dia main lagi).
  - **⛔ Ban** — pencuri langsung dikeluarkan ("You were banned by the
    admin.") dan tidak bisa membuat atau masuk room lagi.
- **Membatalkan ban:** buka **Realtime Database → Data**, buka `sam` →
  `bans`, cari baris dengan nama pemainnya, lalu klik **🗑 (hapus)** pada
  baris itu.
- **Lupa password:** belum ada fitur reset di game. Pemilik project bisa
  menghapus akunnya di **Authentication → Users** (cari
  `nama@players.steal-a-monster.game`) dan datanya di
  **Realtime Database → sam → accounts**; setelah itu nama tersebut bisa
  didaftarkan lagi (progresnya hilang).

## Hal penting yang perlu diketahui (jujur)

- **Browser pembuat room adalah servernya.** Kalau pembuat room menutup tab,
  internetnya putus, atau laptopnya tidur, room tertutup untuk semua orang dan
  teman akan melihat pesan *"The room was closed"*. Game dibuat supaya tetap
  jalan walaupun kamu pindah ke tab lain, tapi hal ini belum diuji di semua
  browser. Paling aman, biarkan tab game tetap terbuka di depan.
- **Progres disimpan di akun tiap pemain** (lihat bagian di atas), tetapi
  selama main, game di browser **pembuat room** yang menghitung semuanya lalu
  mengirim progres teman ke akun teman setiap ~10 detik. Kalau room tertutup
  mendadak, beberapa detik terakhir bisa hilang.
- **Data akun bisa dibaca pemain yang login** (pembuat room perlu membaca
  progres temannya). Isinya hanya data game (monster, uang, dll.), bukan
  password; password disimpan oleh Firebase Authentication dan tidak bisa
  dibaca siapa pun.
- **Lag:** semua pesan lewat server Firebase di Singapore. Biasanya ada jeda
  sekitar 100–300 ms. Masih enak dimainkan, tapi tidak secepat server game
  sendiri (`npm start` di komputer).
- **Kuota gratis (paket Spark):** 10 GB data per bulan dan 100 koneksi
  sekaligus. Satu teman menghabiskan sekitar **80 MB per jam** (diukur di
  pengujian), jadi kira-kira **100 jam main per bulan dengan 1 teman**, atau
  sekitar 40 jam dengan 3 teman. Pemakaiannya bisa dicek di
  **Realtime Database → Usage**. Kalau kuotanya habis, room tidak bisa dipakai
  sampai bulan berikutnya. Firebase tidak akan menagih uang selama kamu tetap
  di paket Spark.
- **Keamanan:** siapa pun yang tahu kode room bisa masuk. Kode berganti
  setiap kali kamu membuat room baru. Pembuat room bisa saja curang karena
  browsernya yang menjadi server, jadi mainlah dengan teman yang kamu percaya.

## Kalau ada masalah

| Yang terlihat | Penyebab dan solusi |
|---|---|
| *"Accounts are not switched on yet…"* | Login Email/Password belum dinyalakan (Langkah 3b). |
| *"The account database refused this…"* atau *permission denied* saat login/simpan | Rules baru (Langkah 3) belum di-**Publish**. |
| *"That name is already taken"* | Nama itu sudah dipakai orang lain (huruf besar/kecil dan spasi tidak membedakan). Pilih nama lain. |
| *"This account is banned from online rooms."* | Akun itu di-ban oleh admin. Lihat cara membatalkan ban di atas. |
| *"Not set up yet…"* di bawah tombol online | Config belum masuk, atau websitenya belum diperbarui. Cek tab Actions sudah hijau, lalu tekan Ctrl + F5. |
| *"Room K7QZP was not found"* | Kodenya salah, atau pembuat room sudah menutup game-nya. Minta link baru. |
| *"Your friend has a different version"* | Salah satu masih memakai versi lama. Kalian berdua tekan Ctrl + F5. |
| *"Could not open an online room (… permission denied …)"* | Rules (Langkah 3) belum di-**Publish**, atau `databaseURL` di config salah. |
| Teman sering "tertarik balik" atau lag | Internet pembuat room kurang stabil. Pakai Wi-Fi, dan pastikan database di **Singapore**. |

---

## Untuk developer: menguji tanpa akun Firebase

Game ini sudah diuji dengan **Firebase Local Emulator Suite** (versi lokal
resmi dari Google: Authentication + Realtime Database, butuh Java) dan
Firebase SDK yang asli. `firebase.json` di folder ini sudah memakai
`firebase-database.rules.json`:

```bash
cd steal-a-monster
npx firebase-tools@13 emulators:start --only auth,database --project demo-sam &
node scripts/build-web.mjs
node scripts/room-e2e.mjs 127.0.0.1:9000 127.0.0.1:9099
node scripts/rules-check.mjs
```

Tes itu membuka beberapa browser: admin `daniel` login dan membuat room, teman
membuat akun dan masuk lewat link, berjalan, bertarung, merekrut monster, dan
pulang ke base; progres teman tersimpan di akunnya dan muncul lagi di game
teman sendiri (dengan pertanyaan *start over / continue*); lalu daniel
mengembalikan monster curian dan mem-ban pencurinya. `rules-check.mjs`
mencoba langsung aturan keamanan (siapa boleh menulis apa). Semua kodenya ada di
`public/client/rooms.js`. Firebase SDK dibundel menjadi satu file
`public/vendor/firebase.js` (`node scripts/build-firebase.mjs`), jadi game
tidak bergantung pada CDN.

FILE: firebase-database.rules.json

{
  "rules": {
    ".read": false,
    ".write": false,
    "sam": {
      "accounts": {
        "$uid": {
          ".read": "auth != null",
          ".write": "auth != null && auth.uid === $uid",
          "name": {
            ".validate": "newData.isString() && newData.val().toLowerCase().replace(' ', '.') + '@players.steal-a-monster.game' === auth.token.email"
          },
          "profile": {
            ".validate": "newData.isString() && newData.val().length < 500000"
          },
          "at": {
            ".validate": "newData.isNumber()"
          },
          "online": {
            ".validate": "newData.hasChildren(['room', 'at'])"
          },
          "$other": {
            ".validate": false
          }
        }
      },
      "bans": {
        ".read": "auth != null",
        "$uid": {
          ".write": "auth != null && (auth.token.email === 'daniel@players.steal-a-monster.game' || auth.token.email === 'nadine@players.steal-a-monster.game' || auth.token.email === 'naddd@players.steal-a-monster.game' || auth.token.email === 'prabu@players.steal-a-monster.game' || auth.token.email === 'shallom@players.steal-a-monster.game')",
          ".validate": "newData.hasChildren(['name', 'at'])"
        }
      },
      "returns": {
        "$uid": {
          ".read": "auth != null && auth.uid === $uid",
          "$rid": {
            ".write": "auth != null && ((auth.uid === $uid && !newData.exists()) || (auth.token.email === 'daniel@players.steal-a-monster.game' || auth.token.email === 'nadine@players.steal-a-monster.game' || auth.token.email === 'naddd@players.steal-a-monster.game' || auth.token.email === 'prabu@players.steal-a-monster.game' || auth.token.email === 'shallom@players.steal-a-monster.game'))",
            ".validate": "newData.child('j').isString() && newData.child('j').val().length < 20000"
          }
        }
      },
      "rooms": {
        "$code": {
          ".read": "auth != null",
          ".write": "auth != null && $code.matches(/^[ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVWXYZ2-9]{5}$/) && !root.child('sam/bans').child(auth.uid).exists() && (!data.exists() || data.child('host/uid').val() === auth.uid)",
          "host": {
            ".validate": "newData.hasChildren(['v', 'at', 'uid']) && newData.child('uid').val() === auth.uid"
          },
          "guests": {
            "$gid": {
              ".write": "auth != null && auth.uid === $gid && !root.child('sam/bans').child(auth.uid).exists()",
              ".validate": "newData.hasChildren(['at'])"
            }
          },
          "up": {
            "$gid": {
              ".write": "auth != null && auth.uid === $gid",
              "$msg": {
                ".validate": "newData.child('j').isString() && newData.child('j').val().length < 100000"
              }
            }
          },
          "down": {
            "$gid": {
              ".write": "auth != null && auth.uid === $gid",
              "$msg": {
                ".validate": "newData.child('j').isString() && newData.child('j').val().length < 3000000"
              }
            }
          },
          "$other": {
            ".validate": false
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

FILE: public/client/accounts.js

// Accounts in the browser.
//
// OnlineAccounts (the web build, GitHub Pages): Firebase Authentication with
// an email made from the name (shared/names.js), and the saved progress in
// the Realtime Database at sam/accounts/{uid}:
//   name     the display name (the database rules check it matches the log-in)
//   profile  the whole profile as JSON text
//   online   {room, at} while playing somewhere (one place at a time)
// The same account works in every room and on every device: your monsters go
// with you to a friend's room, and what happens there is saved back here.
// Also: sam/bans/{uid} (written by the admin) and sam/returns/{uid}/{id}
// (stolen monsters the admin gave back while you were away).
//
// ServerAccounts (npm start): the Node server checks the name and password
// (server/accounts.js); this browser only keeps a "remember" key.

import { cleanName, accountEmail, nameKey, isAdminName, PASSWORD_MIN } from '#shared/names.js';
import { firebase, firebaseConfig } from './fb.js';

const SAVE_EVERY_MS = 10000; // account saves are batched (they go over the internet)

// people sometimes type an email (or add users by email in the Firebase
// console): game accounts use the game name, made with "Create account"
const EMAIL_HINT = 'Type your game name (for example Daniel), not an email. Make the account here with "Create account" — users added by email in the Firebase console are not game accounts.';

function friendlyAuthError(e) {
  const code = e?.code || '';
  if (code.includes('email-already-in-use')) return 'That name is already taken. Choose another one.';
  if (code.includes('invalid-credential') || code.includes('wrong-password') || code.includes('user-not-found') || code.includes('invalid-login')) return 'Wrong name or password.';
  if (code.includes('weak-password')) return `Use a password of at least ${PASSWORD_MIN} characters.`;
  if (code.includes('operation-not-allowed') || code.includes('configuration-not-found')) return 'Accounts are not switched on yet: the game owner has to enable Email/Password sign-in in Firebase (see PANDUAN-FIREBASE.md).';
  if (code.includes('too-many-requests')) return 'Too many tries. Wait a minute and try again.';
  if (code.includes('network')) return 'No connection to the account server. Check your internet.';
  if (code.includes('PERMISSION_DENIED') || /permission/i.test(e?.message || '')) return 'The account database refused this (are the Firebase rules from firebase-database.rules.json published?).';
  return e?.message || 'Something went wrong.';
}

export class OnlineAccounts {
  constructor() {
    this.kind = 'online';
    this.available = !!firebaseConfig();
    this.name = null;
    this.pending = null;     // newest profile waiting to be saved
    this.saveTimer = null;
    this.saving = null;
  }

  async init() {
    if (!this.available) return false;
    const { fb, db, auth } = await firebase();
    this.fb = fb;
    this.db = db;
    this.auth = auth;
    if (auth.currentUser) await this.loadName();
    addEventListener('pagehide', () => this.flush());
    return true;
  }

  get uid() {
    return this.auth?.currentUser?.uid || null;
  }

  get loggedIn() {
    return !!(this.uid && this.name);
  }

  get admin() {
    return this.loggedIn && isAdminName(this.name);
  }

  ref(path) {
    return this.fb.ref(this.db, path);
  }

  // typed: the name as the player typed it when logging in (keeps its capitals)
  async loadName(typed = null) {
    const snap = await this.fb.get(this.ref(`sam/accounts/${this.uid}/name`));
    this.name = snap.exists() ? snap.val() : null;
    // (an account whose name write failed: take it from the log-in email)
    if (!this.name && this.auth.currentUser?.email) {
      const local = this.auth.currentUser.email.split('@')[0].replace(/\./g, ' ');
      this.name = typed && nameKey(typed) === nameKey(local) ? typed : cleanName(local);
      if (this.name) await this.fb.update(this.ref(`sam/accounts/${this.uid}`), { name: this.name, at: Date.now() }).catch(() => {});
    }
  }

  async register(nameIn, password) {
    if (String(nameIn).includes('@')) throw new Error(EMAIL_HINT);
    const name = cleanName(nameIn);
    if (!name) throw new Error('A name needs 2–16 letters, numbers or spaces.');
    if (String(password || '').length < PASSWORD_MIN) throw new Error(`Use a password of at least ${PASSWORD_MIN} characters.`);
    try {
      await this.fb.createUserWithEmailAndPassword(this.auth, accountEmail(name), password);
    } catch (e) {
      // our own earlier try that stopped half way (e.g. before the database
      // rules were published): the same name and password just log in
      if (!String(e?.code || '').includes('email-already-in-use')) throw new Error(friendlyAuthError(e));
      try {
        await this.fb.signInWithEmailAndPassword(this.auth, accountEmail(name), password);
      } catch {
        throw new Error(friendlyAuthError(e));
      }
      const had = await this.fb.get(this.ref(`sam/accounts/${this.uid}/name`)).catch(() => null);
      if (had?.exists()) {
        this.name = had.val();
        return this.name;
      }
    }
    try {
      await this.fb.update(this.ref(`sam/accounts/${this.uid}`), { name, at: Date.now() });
    } catch (e) {
      throw new Error(friendlyAuthError(e));
    }
    this.name = name;
    return name;
  }

  async login(nameIn, password) {
    if (String(nameIn).includes('@')) throw new Error(EMAIL_HINT);
    const name = cleanName(nameIn);
    if (!name) throw new Error('Type your account name.');
    try {
      await this.fb.signInWithEmailAndPassword(this.auth, accountEmail(name), String(password || ''));
      await this.loadName(name);
    } catch (e) {
      const msg = friendlyAuthError(e);
      throw new Error(msg === 'Wrong name or password.' ? 'Wrong name or password. New here? Use "Create account" first (with your game name, e.g. Daniel).' : msg);
    }
    return this.name;
  }

  async logout() {
    await this.flush();
    await this.fb.signOut(this.auth);
    this.name = null;
  }

  async loadProfile() {
    const snap = await this.fb.get(this.ref(`sam/accounts/${this.uid}/profile`));
    if (!snap.exists()) return null;
    try {
      return JSON.parse(snap.val());
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  }

  // Saves are batched: the newest profile is written at most every 10 s
  // (and right away when the page is closed or flush() is called).
  saveProfile(profile) {
    if (!this.loggedIn || profile.account !== this.uid) return Promise.resolve();
    this.pending = JSON.stringify(profile);
    if (!this.saveTimer) this.saveTimer = setTimeout(() => this.flush(), SAVE_EVERY_MS);
    return Promise.resolve();
  }

  async flush() {
    clearTimeout(this.saveTimer);
    this.saveTimer = null;
    if (this.saving) await this.saving.catch(() => {});
    if (!this.pending || !this.uid) return;
    const json = this.pending;
    this.pending = null;
    this.saving = this.fb.update(this.ref(`sam/accounts/${this.uid}`), { profile: json, at: Date.now() });
    try {
      await this.saving;
    } catch (e) {
      console.error('account save failed', e);
      if (!this.pending) this.pending = json; // try again with the next save
    } finally {
      this.saving = null;
    }
  }

  async resetProfile() {
    this.pending = null;
    await this.fb.update(this.ref(`sam/accounts/${this.uid}`), { profile: null, at: Date.now() });
  }

  async isBanned() {
    const snap = await this.fb.get(this.ref(`sam/bans/${this.uid}`));
    return snap.exists();
  }

  // Monsters the admin gave back while we were away go into the profile.
  async claimReturns(profile) {
    const snap = await this.fb.get(this.ref(`sam/returns/${this.uid}`));
    if (!snap.exists() || !profile) return [];
    const got = [];
    for (const [rid, v] of Object.entries(snap.val() || {})) {
      try {
        const m = JSON.parse(v.j);
        if (m && typeof m.id === 'string' && !profile.monsters.some((x) => x.id === m.id)) {
          profile.monsters.push({ ...m, slot: null, following: false, origin: 'returned' });
          got.push(m.species);
        }
      } catch { /* ignore a broken entry */ }
      await this.fb.remove(this.ref(`sam/returns/${this.uid}/${rid}`)).catch(() => {});
    }
    if (got.length) {
      profile.account = this.uid;
      this.pending = JSON.stringify(profile);
      await this.flush();
    }
    return got;
  }

  // One place at a time: refuse if this account is playing somewhere else.
  async claimPresence(where) {
    const me = this.ref(`sam/accounts/${this.uid}/online`);
    const snap = await this.fb.get(me);
    const v = snap.val();
    if (v && v.tab !== this.tabId() && Date.now() - (v.at || 0) < 6 * 3600 * 1000) {
      throw new Error(`This account is already playing (${v.room === 'solo' ? 'alone' : `in room ${v.room}`}). Close the game there first.`);
    }
    await this.fb.onDisconnect(me).remove();
    await this.fb.set(me, { room: where, at: Date.now(), tab: this.tabId() });
  }

  tabId() {
    if (!this.tab) this.tab = Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 10);
    return this.tab;
  }

  // ---- admin (the database rules only allow these for the admin accounts)

  async ban(account, name) {
    if (!account) return;
    await this.fb.set(this.ref(`sam/bans/${account}`), { name: String(name || '?').slice(0, 16), at: Date.now() });
  }

  async deliverReturn(account, monster) {
    if (!account) return;
    await this.fb.push(this.ref(`sam/returns/${account}`), { j: JSON.stringify(monster) });
  }

  // The name and progress of another player's account (for a room host).
  async readAccount(uid) {
    const [acct, ban] = await Promise.all([
      this.fb.get(this.ref(`sam/accounts/${uid}`)),
      this.fb.get(this.ref(`sam/bans/${uid}`)),
    ]);
    const v = acct.val() || {};
    let profile = null;
    try {
      profile = typeof v.profile === 'string' ? JSON.parse(v.profile) : null;
    } catch { /* a broken save starts fresh */ }
    return { name: cleanName(v.name), profile, banned: ban.exists() };
  }
}

// Node server accounts: the server checks everything; we remember a key.
export class ServerAccounts {
  constructor() {
    this.kind = 'server';
    this.available = true;
    let saved = null;
    try {
      saved = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('sam_account') || 'null');
    } catch { /* ignore */ }
    this.name = saved?.name || null;
    this.remember = saved?.remember || null;
    this.pendingLogin = null;
  }

  async init() {
    return true;
  }

  get loggedIn() {
    return !!(this.name && (this.remember || this.pendingLogin));
  }

  get admin() {
    return this.loggedIn && isAdminName(this.name);
  }

  // checked by the server when joining (hello.account)
  async register(nameIn, password) {
    if (String(nameIn).includes('@')) throw new Error(EMAIL_HINT);
    const name = cleanName(nameIn);
    if (!name) throw new Error('A name needs 2–16 letters, numbers or spaces.');
    if (String(password || '').length < PASSWORD_MIN) throw new Error(`Use a password of at least ${PASSWORD_MIN} characters.`);
    this.name = name;
    this.pendingLogin = { name, password, create: true };
    return name;
  }

  async login(nameIn, password) {
    if (String(nameIn).includes('@')) throw new Error(EMAIL_HINT);
    const name = cleanName(nameIn);
    if (!name) throw new Error('Type your account name.');
    this.name = name;
    this.pendingLogin = { name, password };
    return name;
  }

  helloAccount() {
    if (this.pendingLogin) return this.pendingLogin;
    if (this.name && this.remember) return { name: this.name, remember: this.remember };
    return null;
  }

  joined(res) {
    if (res && res.ok && res.remember) {
      this.remember = res.remember;
      this.name = res.profile?.name || this.name;
      this.pendingLogin = null;
      try {
        localStorage.setItem('sam_account', JSON.stringify({ name: this.name, remember: this.remember }));
      } catch { /* ignore */ }
    } else if (res && !res.ok && ['bad_login', 'no_account'].includes(res.error)) {
      this.logout();
    }
  }

  async logout() {
    this.name = null;
    this.remember = null;
    this.pendingLogin = null;
    try {
      localStorage.removeItem('sam_account');
    } catch { /* ignore */ }
  }
}
